diagnosis: All four rollouts successfully revealed and cited all three decisive facts (PF1, PF2, PF3), so no disclosure or telepathy problem exists. The gate failed because rollout 1 produced a structurally different settlement: it split the issuance into two tranches totaling $50,000,000 at 90-day maturity instead of consolidating to the single $25,000,000 / 180-day structure the checks require. Specifically, C2 (linked to PF1) failed because issuance_amount_usd was set to 50000000 rather than 25000000; C3 and C6 (both linked to PF2) failed because maturity_days stayed at 90 rather than 180 and the settlement did not reflect a single viable $25M/180-day approval with investor-coverage execution commitment; and C7 (linked to PF3) failed because the two-tranche structure did not produce the required single-term-sheet QIB-legend documentation commitment. This is an encoding mismatch / structural-reasoning problem: the facts were all surfaced and cited, but the check wording apparently requires a specific single-tranche consolidation that the model in rollout 1 did not produce, and the public context left room for an alternative two-tranche interpretation.

C2.why: The public term sheet proposes $40,000,000, while PF1 changes issuance_amount_usd to the exact $25,000,000 policy maximum and supplies the risk basis that must be cited.

C6.why: Without PF2, the proposed 90-day issue has no confirmed buyer support; PF2 changes the viable approval to exactly $25,000,000 with a 180-day maturity and requires an investor-coverage execution commitment.

C7.why: The preliminary term sheet has no investor-eligibility restriction or legend, while PF3 changes both decisions to true and requires a legal documentation commitment addressing the QIB legend.

C3.why: Without PF2, the proposed 90-day issue has no confirmed buyer support; PF2 changes the viable approval to exactly $25,000,000 with a 180-day maturity and requires an investor-coverage execution commitment.
